column1: # *** WHERE SANCHO'S 1791 MARRIAGE ACT CAN PHYSICALLY BE - 14 September 2026. ***
# Built from the Instituto de Estudios Genealogicos del Uruguay's own holdings list, read over plain
# http because its certificate has expired. *** The venue has never had a source *** - the 8 January 1791
# date comes from Apolant ficha 355 and 'Canelones' comes from nowhere. So the question is not 'find the
# Canelones act' but 'which surviving books could hold a marriage on that date'. Four answers, one of
# which is eliminated here and one of which this archive had never considered.

column2: what the IEGU holdings list says

column1: *** CANELONES - Catedral de Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe ***
column2: Baut. y Matr. desde 1775; def. desde 1776. Existen algunas informaciones matrimoniales desde 1776.
column3: *** YES - marriages from 1775, sixteen years before ***
column4: *** Still the leading candidate, and now for a reason beyond habit. *** The 1812 padron records all six children as "naturales del CANELON", the eldest born about 1791. *** And the informaciones matrimoniales series from 1776 is the one in which Sancho has ALREADY been found, giving sworn evidence at somebody else's marriage. ***

column1: *** SAN JOSE DE MAYO - Catedral de San Jose ***
column2: Baut. y Def. desde 1783; *** Matr. desde 1799 ***. Los indices contienen graves errores de lectura del amanuense.
column3: *** NO - marriages begin in 1799, EIGHT YEARS TOO LATE ***
column4: *** RAISED AND ELIMINATED IN ONE STEP, on 14 September 2026. *** San Jose became a candidate the moment the Operativo Patagonia cohort was understood: *** the 41 Asturian founder families - SEVEN OF THEM FROM MORCIN, the concejo where Josefa Fernandez Tresguerras was born in 1778 - founded SAN JOSE, URUGUAY on 1 June 1783, *** not Canelones. So the bride's family very plausibly landed there. *** But the parish has no marriage book before 1799, so a marriage of January 1791 cannot be in it. *** Its baptisms DO run from 1783 and are worth searching for her family's arrival. *** Note the IEGU's own warning that the San Jose indexes carry serious copyist errors - so an index null there would be worth very little. ***

column1: *** MONTEVIDEO - Iglesia Matriz, and its LIBROS CASTRENSES ***
column2: Baut. Matr. desde 1727; Def. desde 1729. Hay tambien *** tres Libros Castrenses con Baut., Matr. y Def. que abarcan el periodo 1781-1814 ***.
column3: *** YES - twice over: the ordinary books from 1727, and the MILITARY books across 1781-1814 ***
column4: *** THIS IS THE LEAD THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER HAD, and it comes from one clause in a holdings list. *** *** SANCHO WAS A SOLDADO. *** The register has called him a soldier since the first day, on the Uruguayan census of 1726-1858. *** A soldier marrying in the Banda Oriental in 1791 has an obvious second home for his act: the CASTRENSE books, kept by the military chaplaincy rather than the parish, *** and those books cover 1781 to 1814 - the whole of his marrying life. *** If the act is not at Canelones, this is where to look next, and nobody has looked. ***

column2: Posee expedientes de *** informacion matrimonial desde 1727 ***, aunque con lagunas en los primeros anos.
column3: *** YES - from 1727, with gaps in the early years ***
column4: *** A THIRD place, and a different KIND of document. *** An informacion matrimonial is the pre-marriage investigation - it routinely gives a Spanish groom's PARENTS, BIRTHPLACE and how long he has been in the country, *** which is more than the marriage act itself usually carries. *** For the questions this archive actually has - Sancho or Francisco, Cordoba or not, who were Felix and Rosalia - *** the investigation would be worth more than the act. ***
